newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria bonds finish week stronger on EMU doubts.
newsitem.headline: Austria bonds finish week stronger on EMU doubts.

text.p: 1600 GMT - Austrian bonds firmed on Friday after a hectic trading day dominated by rumors of a German initiative to postpone Europe's planned single currency. The Bundesbank said it was not aware of such plans.
"Markets are increasingly taking a bet against an early start," said one trader. "It's already partly priced in."
* 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 up 60 bps at 100.90 to yield 5.50 pct (5.58) in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.68/100.78 to yield 5.53/52.
* At the near end, five-year 5.50 percent bond maturing March 2001 up 15 bps at 104.35 to yield 4.37 (4.41) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 104.16/104.26 to yield 4.42/39 percent.
* AGB future up 34 bps at 110.76 on turnover of 1,236 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany steady at one bps, five-year spread up one at minus two.
* Money market rates stable with three-month VIBOR at 3.300 and overnight money just lower at 2.97/3.22.
